_note: Sources for the real people who play the 8 example creators (src/lib/examples.ts). Each creator uses one shoot: a profile photo, a storefront photo and, where the post shows them, a content photo. Files live in design/content/real as <creator>-<source id>.jpg, ungraded (no warm filter). scripts/render-posts.py crops them.

pexels.why: Pexels license, 'What is not allowed': "Don't imply endorsement of your product by people or brands on the imagery." A named creator with a handle and a post promoting a product implies endorsement, fictional product or not.

unsplash_free.why: Terms section 5: the license excludes "People's images if they are recognizable in the Images"; you may need the person's permission.

pixabay.why: No releases; bars misleading or deceptive use and leaves third-party consent to the user.

kaboompics.why: Terms bar use suggesting a depicted person endorses or is involved with something.

canva_free.why: Free Media License bars implying people in an image endorse your product.

istock.why: Content license 3.2 bars commercial and endorsement use only for 'editorial use only' content, which is not model released. Creative images are model and property released and 9.1 warrants the releases for use as the agreement allows. 3.5: sensitive uses need 'Stock photo. Posed by model.'; endorsement is not on that list, but the examples are already labeled as examples, and a 'posed by models' line costs nothing. iStock's library is Non-AI. Standard license covers web use.
istock.price: $12 an image (1 credit), or 10 images a month for $70, as shown on the image pages 2026-10-29

license.also_ok_not_checked_in_depth: Getty creative RF (same terms as iStock), Unsplash+ (warrants publicity rights; only sensitive topics need a 'posed by model' note).

status: shortlisted on iStock, not purchased.
